analysis.title: Paper Tail Risk Is Cheap, And Everyone Just Noticed: Hedge Funds Load Up On Brent Upside, Dealers Face 'Short Gamma' Squeezed
key_insights: December Brent settled at $109.86 on Friday after briefly topping $110 for the first time since May 20, a second straight weekly gain. Drivers were a tanker fire in the Gulf of Oman, a Ukrainian strike on Russia's Ryazan refinery, and an Iranian state TV report of a 'thermal anomaly' near a Saudi pipeline at Yanbu.

Goldman Sachs Research raised its December Brent forecast to $90 from $85 and sees Brent averaging $80 in 2027. It says Persian Gulf exports have 'rebounded close to 2025 levels since late September.'

Robert Quinn on Goldman's futures desk reports that speculative demand for Brent futures accelerated during Oct 6-13 as price gained 5.1%. Managed Money, Other and Non-Reportable accounts bought $4.9bn, a substantial increase in pace from the prior 2 weeks.
Managed Money bought $3.4bn net. New longs were $2.3bn, of which 32% were call initiations, roughly $0.7bn of fresh call exposure in one reporting week (ZeroHedge's arithmetic).

Speculative net length is about $14bn, against about $38bn at the April peak. The Managed Money-only series is about $25bn now versus about $46bn in April. Price is near the war highs while positioning is not, and the 32% call share suggests funds are using options rather than futures to hold the tail.

The buying changed the options surface. Brent's 3-month normalized 25-delta put-call skew cheapened and the ratio of 5-delta to 50-delta call implied vol rose, 'reflecting posturing for extreme price spikes.' Overall implied vol fell, mostly because realized vol fell.
60-day realized vol slid from the mid-50s to the mid-40s and 3-month implied is around 40%, less than half the roughly 84% peak in March (approximate, read off the chart).

Similar flows 'arguably ensued' over Oct 13-16 as Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian energy infrastructure and Israel raised alert levels. Brent added another 4.0% (about 9% compounded across both windows), skew kept cheapening, and 3-month 5-delta calls outperformed.

Quinn writes that dealers and market makers 'seem incrementally shorter gamma, creating some risk of upside amplification should tensions worsen.' Dealers short calls must buy futures as price rises, which can accelerate a move.
The 5-delta/50-delta call vol ratio is about 1.39, up from a late-September low of about 1.24 but well below the roughly 1.79 hit in February (approximate). Tail pricing 'remains far from peak.'

The curve is mixed. December-January Brent declined during the Oct 6-13 buying, which Quinn attributes to the volume of oil including estimated dark flows transiting the Persian Gulf. Only in the last three sessions did the 1-2 spread gain, with the rally larger in longer-dated term structure.

Goldman Research estimates about 4 million bpd of 'dark' shipments on tankers with transponders off. ZeroHedge notes the latest tanker to catch fire was one that Iranian state TV said had 'turned off its tracking systems.'
UBS has Yanbu loadings averaging 1.6mb/d in October, down from 2.7mb/d in September. Riyadh is planning a major expansion of the East-West pipeline.

Goldman Research says a $25 risk premium is boosting spot Brent, up from a 'near-record' $22 cited a week earlier. It expects a shift to surplus starting Q4 2026 driven by Gulf adaptation, more non-Gulf output and demand reductions from high prices.

A $90 December forecast against the $109.86 settle implies a fall of about $20, or about 18%, in ten weeks (ZeroHedge's arithmetic). Goldman warns prices 'may stay high for longer than anticipated' given escalation risk involving the US, Israel and Iran.

ZeroHedge's view is that Goldman's research (premium fades, Brent to $80) and Goldman's desk (funds buying calls, dealers shorter gamma) are on opposite sides. The desk note is a 'solicitation of derivatives business' per its own disclaimer. ZeroHedge will check the next COT update to see whether the call buying continued.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman Research expects Brent to fall to $90 by December and average $80 in 2027 as the risk premium fades and Gulf supply recovers. Goldman's futures desk sees funds buying upside calls and dealers shorter gamma.

macro_indicators.interpretation: First trade above $110 since May 20 and a second straight weekly gain, driven by Gulf supply-disruption headlines.
Implies about an 18% decline from Friday's settle, which depends on Gulf supply recovery and the risk premium fading.
Based on a shift to surplus starting in Q4 2026.
Goldman's estimate of the war premium in spot Brent, which grew $3 in a week even as Goldman expects it to fade.
Less than half the roughly 84% March peak, because realized vol fell while far out-of-the-money upside got more popular.
Lower realized vol pulled overall implied vol down despite call-skew changes.
The Hormuz-bypass route is itself under pressure, which weakens the supply-recovery case.

risk_factors: Escalation of the conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran, which Goldman says could keep prices high for longer than anticipated
Attacks on Hormuz-bypass infrastructure (Fujairah, Yanbu, the Saudi East-West line)
Near-record-low inventories and a persistent diesel squeeze, which the IEA says will last into 2027
Dealer short-gamma hedging amplifying an upside move
Record tanker rates and a refining system with no slack, so new supply hits have outsized effects
The Goldman base case relies on about 4 million bpd of dark flows that Iran can apparently track

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's futures desk reports funds buying Brent calls (32% of new longs), dealers incrementally shorter gamma, and attacks on Gulf bypass routes, so upside could amplify if tensions worsen. The risk premium rose to $25 from $22 in a week.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman Research expects Gulf supply to recover, a surplus from Q4 2026, a $90 December price and an $80 2027 average. Implied vol is about 40% versus 84% in March, and positioning and tail pricing are far below the April and February peaks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: For the bear case: continued Gulf attacks on bypass infrastructure and escalation involving the US, Israel and Iran. For the bull case: dark flows keep arriving and Houthi attacks stop, so calls decay.

theme_stances.key_argument: Goldman Research expects the risk premium to fade and Brent to fall as Gulf supply recovers and a surplus emerges.
